content_sections.heading: Yadgir District Court Important Dates
content_sections.text: Note: The notifications do not specify the exact dates for the typing/proficiency test, written test or interview. Eligible candidates' lists and call letters will be published on the district court website and communicated by SMS/e-mail.

content_sections.heading: Yadgir District Court Vacancy 2026 (Post-wise)
content_sections.text: 5 Typist 4 Typist Copyist 9 Process Server 5 Peon Note: *The PwD post under Process Server is earmarked specifically for candidates with low-vision/blindness. If no eligible candidate with this specific disability is available, the post will be carried forward to a future recruitment rather than filled by a candidate with a different disability. Across all four posts, if suitable candidates are not available under the Women or Ex-servicemen reservation, those posts will be filled from other eligible candidates of the same reserved category, as per Government Order No. DPAR 34 SENE 95, Bengaluru, dated 15 July 1996.

content_sections.heading: Yadgir District Court Selection Process
content_sections.text: A typing proficiency test is conducted – candidates type a 15-minute dictated passage in both Kannada and English on a typewriter/computer, as directed. The proficiency test carries a maximum of 100 marks each in Kannada and English; a candidate must score at least 50 marks in each language to qualify. An interview carrying 10 marks follows for qualified candidates; final selection is based on marks obtained in the interview. Merit rank is based on the percentage of marks scored in the SSLC or equivalent qualifying examination. Candidates are shortlisted for interview at a ratio of 1 post to 25 candidates (1:25), based on highest marks, for each category of vacancy notified. The interview carries 10 marks; final selection is based on marks obtained at interview. Merit rank is based on the percentage of marks scored in the SSLC or equivalent qualifying examination. Candidates are shortlisted for interview at a ratio of 1 post to 10 candidates (1:10), based on highest marks, for each category of vacancy notified. The interview carries 10 marks; final selection is based on marks obtained at interview. Selection for all four posts is made through direct recruitment under the Karnataka Subordinate Courts (Ministerial and Other Posts) (Recruitment) Rules, 1982, as amended in 2007 and 2021. Selected candidates undergo a probation period of 2 years under the Karnataka Civil Services (Probation) Rules, 1977, extendable if required.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for Yadgir District Court Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Visit the district court's official recruitment portal: yadgir.dcourts.gov.in/online-recruitment . Select the notification for the post you wish to apply for (Typist / Typist Copyist / Process Server / Peon) and fill in the online application form completely. Upload a recent passport-size photograph (white background, 3.5cm x 5cm, max 50KB, JPG) and a scanned signature on white paper in black ballpoint pen (2.5cm x 7.5cm, max 25KB, JPG). Upload all required certificates as clear, readable PDF scans (see Documents section below). Pay the application fee online only – via net banking, credit card, debit card or UPI through the link provided on the portal. Preview the completed application carefully before final submission – once submitted, the application cannot be withdrawn or edited. Take a printout of the submitted application for your records, and note your application number for future reference. Important: Only online applications submitted through the official portal are accepted – applications sent by any other means (post, e-mail, in person) will not be considered. A candidate submitting more than one application for the same post will have only the last submitted application considered.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required (Upload at Application Stage)
content_sections.text: Birth-date proof: SSLC/equivalent examination certificate (for Peon & Process Server) or second PUC/equivalent examination certificate (for Typist & Typist Copyist) Marks card of SSLC/equivalent (Peon & Process Server) or second PUC/equivalent (Typist & Typist Copyist) Typing/proficiency examination certificate(s) – senior grade for Typist, junior grade for Typist Copyist (or diploma in commerce/equivalent) Caste and income certificate (only if claiming reservation) 371-J local-cadre eligibility certificate Other reservation certificates, only if applicable: Rural reservation certificate (Form-2, class 1–10 study in rural areas), Kannada-medium study certificate (Form-2, class 1–10), disability certificate, project-displaced-persons certificate, ex-servicemen (discharge) certificate Passport-size photograph and scanned signature in the prescribed size and format NOC from the current employer, for candidates already in Government service At the interview stage , shortlisted candidates must additionally bring: original documents corresponding to every certificate uploaded online; a photo ID (voter ID/Aadhaar/PAN/ration card/passport/driving licence); and three character certificates – one from the head of the institution last attended (with academic record), and two separate certificates from two unrelated, respectable persons well acquainted with the candidate.

content_sections.heading: Important Conditions
content_sections.text: Application fee: General – ₹200; Category-2A/2B/3A/3B – ₹100; SC/ST/Category-1/persons with disability – ₹50. Fee must be paid online only; cheques, demand drafts, postal orders and money orders are not accepted, and applications with unpaid fee will be rejected. Reservation-category certificates must be in the prescribed format: SC/ST candidates – Form D; Category-1 candidates – Form E; Category-2A/2B/3A/3B candidates – Form F. Only caste and income certificates obtained specifically for employment purposes are considered – certificates obtained for education or other benefits are not accepted. Rural-reservation candidates must have studied class 1 to 10 entirely in a rural area, certified in Form-2, countersigned by the Field/Range Education Officer and the concerned Tahsildar. Kannada-medium reservation candidates must have studied class 1 to 10 entirely in Kannada medium, similarly certified in Form-2. Candidates belonging to SC/ST/Category-1/2A/2B/3A/3B must compulsorily submit the rural-reservation certificate to claim that quota; failing this, they become ineligible for the rural quota. Disability-quota candidates must hold a certificate from the competent authority as per Government Order No. CASuE 115 SENE 2005 dated 19.11.2005, valid as on the application deadline. Candidates already in Government service must submit a No-Objection Certificate (NOC) before the final selection order is issued. Local-cadre (371-J) candidates for the Kalyana Karnataka region must submit an eligibility certificate from the competent authority in the format prescribed under Government Order No. DPAR/06/PLC/2012 dated 06.11.2013. Caste, category and other reservation certificates obtained after the application deadline will not be considered. If any discrepancy is found between the uploaded documents and the original documents produced at interview/verification, the candidate forfeits their candidature. If a candidate fails to produce the original documents corresponding to the uploaded certificates at the time of verification, their application will not be accepted thereafter. If original documents on verification do not match a claimed reservation category, that reservation claim is cancelled and the candidate is considered only under the General category, if otherwise eligible. Reservation-category certificates submitted in a non-prescribed format will not be considered. If a candidate holding a qualification higher than SSLC/10th standard does not disclose that fact and related details, they will be liable for penal action. The category/reservation entered in the online application is final; requests for change thereafter will not be considered under any circumstances. Merely being called for interview confers no right to appointment; the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Yadgir is not bound to select any candidate found unsuitable. faq.question: Q1. How many total posts are there across all four notifications?
faq.answer: 23 posts in all – 5 Typist, 4 Typist Copyist, 9 Process Server and 5 Peon, in the Kalyana Karnataka Vrinda (Local Cadre) of Yadgir district courts.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: 30 September 2026, 11:59 PM, for all four posts; the fee must be paid by 1 October 2026.

faq.question: Q3. Can I apply offline or by post?
faq.answer: No. Only online applications through yadgir.dcourts.gov.in/online-recruitment are accepted.

faq.question: Q4. What is the educational qualification for Typist and Typist Copyist?
faq.answer: Second PUC/3-year diploma/equivalent, plus a typing qualification – senior grade (Typist) or junior grade (Typist Copyist) in Kannada and English, or a commerce diploma/equivalent.

faq.question: Q5. What is the educational qualification for Process Server and Peon?
faq.answer: SSLC or an equivalent examination; a driving licence is preferred for Process Server, and the ability to read/write Kannada is required for Peon.

faq.question: Q6. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: Minimum 18 years; maximum 40 years (General) to 45 years (SC/ST/Category-1), plus a one-time 5-year relaxation for all categories under a 2026 Government Order, and further relaxation for ex-servicemen and persons with disability.

faq.question: Q7. How is selection done for Typist/Typist Copyist versus Process Server/Peon?
faq.answer: Typist and Typist Copyist candidates take a typing proficiency test (100 marks each in Kannada & English, 50 minimum each to qualify) followed by a 10-mark interview. Process Server and Peon candidates are ranked on SSLC/equivalent marks and shortlisted for a 10-mark interview at a 1:25 (Process Server) or 1:10 (Peon) ratio.

faq.question: Q8. What is the application fee?
faq.answer: ₹200 for General category, ₹100 for Category-2A/2B/3A/3B, and ₹50 for SC/ST/Category-1/persons with disability, payable online only.
